issues.detail: The Greek 'κατηγωνισαντο βασιλειας' refers to 'overcoming kingdoms' (kingdoms as in realms/reigns), but the Vietnamese 'thắng các nước' translates to 'won/defeated countries'. While similar, 'vương quốc' is the more precise term for 'basileias' to avoid confusion with modern nation-states.

The Greek 'επετυχον επαγγελιων' implies 'having obtained/attained the promises'. The Vietnamese 'được những lời hứa' (received the promises) loses the nuance of 'attaining' or 'winning' the promises as a result of their faith.
